findings.diagnosis: The prompt under-penalises cuts that split a predicate from the phrase that completes it: it treats positions before the object/clausal complement as acceptable, producing standalone prefixes that the continuation contradicts or that cannot be interpreted on their own.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_1294','en_us_1113','en_us_1118','en_us_738','en_us_399','en_us_990','en_us_1570','en_us_292']: these cases all show the policy keeping a cut that separates a verb or verbal phrase from its required object or clausal complement (e.g. 'said' + 'that ...', 'drops' + 'the envelope', 'directed ... to ...', 'would need' + 'to have ...', 'will cause' + 'cracks ...').
findings.type_predicate: A candidate cut sits immediately after a main verb or auxiliary (including modals and light verbs) whose clause is continued by a direct object NP, a complementizer-introduced clause (that/which/who), an infinitival 'to' complement, or a verb-argument prepositional phrase.

edit.text: Do not cut between a predicate (main verb or auxiliary+verb) and its required object or clausal complement (direct-object NP, 'that/which/who' clause, 'to' infinitive, or verb-argument prepositional phrase).
